subject: Pilot qualification: handling extended visit history — model options & next steps
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@carevista.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: demo & long visit histories

Thanks for the demo this morning — good overview. Couple of clarifying points from our side that will determine next steps on procurement and a small pilot:

1) Data shape: patient timelines average ~12 visits but ~10% have 60+ visits, with each visit containing free-text notes and structured meds/labs.
2) Primary ask: summarize clinical course across all visits and extract discrete problem list items with provenance (visit date).
3) Concern: we saw examples where the model dropped early visit context when history grew long — want to understand truncation risk and quality regressions.

Can you share recommended model tiers, any benchmark references for long-history summarization, and an initial prompt set we can run on a 1–2 week pilot? Also, what would a minimal mutual action plan look like?

Thanks — happy to sync again next week.

—Samir
Director, Product 
CareVista

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@carevista.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo & long visit histories

Samir — thanks for the notes and great questions. Recap and proposal below.

Quick recap of risks we saw in your sample:
- Truncation of early visits when using 32k-token models with naïve windowing; drops usually happen past ~40k total tokens in our tests.
- Summarization fidelity drops when the model is asked to both summarize narrative and provide structured problem lists without explicit separation.

Recommended model strategy (initial):
- Tier A (latency-sensitive): a 32k token LLM quantized variant (best for near-real-time UIs). Good for summarization where you can accept light compression.
- Tier B (high-fidelity): 65k/100k context model (higher cost) for full-visit, provenance-aware summarization and extraction. Use for nightly batch jobs or canary outputs.
- Fallback policy: route to Tier B when input token count > 40k or when a provenance-flag is requested.

Benchmark & artifacts I attached: prompt set v1 (carevista_prompt_set_v1.json) and a short deck with benchmark links (cv_benchmark_links.md). The Drive link in the metadata has the raw notebooks and example runs.

Initial mutual action plan (MAP) — rough 4-week pilot:
- Week 0: exchange full sample dataset + redacted PHI mapping (CareVista).
- Week 1: Redwood runs baseline evals (compression / truncation sweeps) using the attached prompt set and returns per-case failure modes.
- Week 2: Jointly review failures; Redwood proposes prompt & routing adjustments and a two-model configuration (Tier A/B) for the pilot.
- Week 3: Small canary (50–100 records) with provenance checks; measure F1 on extracted problems and manual fidelity score on summaries.
- Week 4: Outcome review, next steps for integration (Dedicated capacity) and pricing estimate.

Asks for you: share a small redacted sample (10–30 records) and a contact on your engineering side for S3 access or a temporary bucket. Also confirm whether nightly batch vs interactive latency matters more for you — that changes the recommended default.

I flagged Priyom here to help design the eval harness and Neha for overall pilot scope and SLA conversation.

Next availability: I have 11–2pm PT tomorrow for a 30-minute sync.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: carevista_prompt_set_v1.json, cv_benchmark_links.md

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@carevista.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo & long visit histories

Samir — thanks for the detailed ask. A couple of operational notes from an eval/quality perspective: 

- Evaluation metrics: beyond token-level F1 for extraction, we recommend a human-rated "summary fidelity" rubric (0–3) that tracks missing early-history facts, hallucinated events, and date-provenance accuracy. We'll include that rubric in the Drive artifacts.
- Truncation mitigation we propose: prefix-space caching + selective recall. Practically, that means keeping a condensed representation (visit-level summaries) in the prompt for early visits and streaming full text for recent visits. This reduces token usage with minimal fidelity loss for chronology-sensitive claims.
- Prompt engineering: separate the steps — (1) generate visit-level synopses, (2) produce consolidated timeline + problem list with visit dates sourced to synopses. The attached prompt set follows that pattern.

Operational ask: please give us two example records that represent the 10% high-length tail (60+ visits) and two median-length records so we can tune heuristics. We'll run the first sweep on both Tier A and Tier B models and return a short table of failure modes.

I'll coordinate the rubric and the eval notebook (Priyom will run the jobs). Ben — please capture budget expectations from procurement so we can size Dedicated if it looks necessary.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference

Ben / Neha — thanks, that plan looks reasonable. We can provide the sample set (2 long-tail + 2 median) by COB Monday and will open a temporary S3 bucket for Redwood. Procurement: I have a rough budget band for a pilot, will pass that to Ben privately.

Let's lock the 30-minute sync for tomorrow at 11:30am PT to confirm S3 details and the rubric.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — excited to see the first sweep results.

—Samir
